checks_run.procedure: Read D-278, D-279, ADR-0064 Amendment 5 (A5.1-A5.7), schedule-explained.mjs, the transfer-drill.sh D7/D9 changes, the harness re-check and reconcile.ts's output section, and check the rule against D-278 clause by clause. Look for ways around it: a user 'run now' of a scheduled job (apps/api/src/modules/jobs/operations.ts), a scheduleSlotKey retry key, engine ticks, READ COMMITTED races between the recheck and a starter job, and an 'N changed' count without a key line.
checks_run.command: read-only source review (sed/grep) of the files named
checks_run.expected: The rule explains only schedule-triggered executions with no initiating user, a key naming an enabled job_schedule slot inside (W0-60 s, W1] on the target clock, created in the window, with their own worker event, one per slot, plus their action results and events. Everything else stays unexplained. Read only. No job paused. Listed in the report. Disclosed.
checks_run.actual: Matches D-278 and A5.2 exactly. Gate 0 accepts only the attachment, informational, two per-table, 'unexplained added' key and final lines. Any 'unexplained changed', missing, expected-but-not, chain-depth or other-table line makes the rule not applicable. A changed count with no key line can only be audit-explained rows, so nothing is hidden. The stage runs BEGIN ... READ ONLY with default_transaction_read_only=on, verifies that, and never writes job_schedule. reconcile-d9.json keeps the real exit 4. Observations, none a defect: (a) A user 'run now' (job.repair, ADM_TECH) sends the schedule's job, and its key minute is the request minute. It can only match S6 within a slot minute, and its own job_schedule.run_now audit and outbox rows stay subject to the unchanged mode 2. Two executions for one slot fail uniqueness. (b) The recheck runs at READ COMMITTED and a starter writes in 2 transactions. A starter that commits during the recheck can make the stage see a result missing from U_r, giving a false D9 FAIL ('not in the recheck's unexplained list'). That is strict, never loose; I did not observe it. The documented recovery (re-run the drill) applies. (c) A5.7 residuals: engine ticks are not covered, and timing rests on pg-boss 11.0.0. Both are disclosed in the register notes and the ADR. Any looseness would re-open D-278. I found none.

checks_run.procedure: My own probe, written independently of the shipped tests, imports schedule-explained.mjs from the clone. It drives stage(), and through it gate0() and explain(), with 4 positive controls and 38 attempts to make the rule explain a write it must not.
checks_run.expected: Controls pass. Every adversarial case FAILs, with the A5.4 reason for the first violated condition.
checks_run.actual: Run 2: 42 cases, 42 as expected, exit 0. Run 1 exited 1 with one BAD case, N22: the stage refused (pass=false), but my probe expected both listed executions to fail with 'has 2 executions'. My fixture had given the second execution no audit events, so it failed S9 first. That was a probe construction error, not a product result. I gave X2 its own events and re-ran, and both failures were then uniqueness (log kept as f971-adversarial-probe-run1-probe-bug.log). Refused as required: an initiating user; run_as user; event or request triggers on a scheduled code; no or a disabled schedule row; a key code different from trigger_code; keys with seconds or event-style suffixes; key minute +2 min; slots before the window, exactly at W0-60 s, or after W1; created before W0 or after W1; events carrying a user, from the API, at or below the baseline, or not at the current version; a package row; a second execution for a slot, listed or not; a stray result; a result event from another job; a non-starter_handler action; tables approval, reporting_period or approval_step (child_of); unexplained changed; an attachment mismatch; a wrong table count; recheck exit 1; a chain-depth line; 20 keys; a key line before any table; no execution key; MON cron; an unknown timezone. Passing controls: the F-DG7-971 shape, key = slot + 1 min, recheck exit 0, and a daily '10 0 * * *' Asia/Riyadh slot at 21:10Z the day before.
